fixer.title: menubar: show open menus above the quick input

cases.mechanism: Disposing a MenuBar with an open, focused menu could synchronously emit focus loss before host listeners were disposed; CustomMenubarControl could re-enter setupCustomMenubar and allocate/register a replacement during the enclosing DisposableStore.clear(), losing normal lifecycle ownership and retaining the replacement DOM/listeners.
cases.symptom: Repeated menubar replacement while a menu is open could leak reconstructed MenuBar instances, DOM nodes, event listeners, and action/menu state, causing retained-memory growth across reinstallation cycles.
cases.fixedBehavior: The new isOpen branch invokes cleanupCustomMenu() before super.dispose(). cleanupCustomMenu first moves focus back to the menu button inside the same container, removes the holder/widget, and clears menu disposables without transitioning focusState, so host focus listeners cannot reconstruct the menubar during disposal. super.dispose() then tears down the remaining listeners and emitters once, bounding the lifecycle to the single instance being disposed.
cases.evidence: Before this PR, MenuBar.dispose() entered super.dispose() while an open menu still owned the focused holder/widget. menuDisposables is the first registered disposable (line 91), so super disposal tears down that focused menu before the container FOCUS_OUT listener and _onFocusStateChange emitter are disposed. The focus-out path calls setUnfocusedState(), which fires onFocusStateChange(false); CustomMenubarControl's listener at menubarControl.ts:527 responds by calling setupCustomMenubar(true) when pendingFirstTimeUpdate is set, re-entering reinstallDisposables.clear() and constructing another MenuBar during disposal. The added test exercises open-menu disposal and verifies that no focus/visibility host events escape. This is a concrete re-entrant allocation/listener retention path, not merely an optimization label.
